ruling.recommended_action: Record the RD-1 breach (F3) on the driver's file without monetary recovery; no refund, no account flag — the fare was billed on the optimal 16.5 km fixed quote and RD-6's predicate is unmet.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeX fixed-quote trip (Bugis Junction → Jurong East MRT) and the trace settles it as a non-metered service, so mileage driven during the trip does not enter the fare [F4][F6][RD-2]. The fare record confirms this: billed distance 16.5 km equals the optimal route, distance line $23.31 on 16.53 km, waiting $0.00, platform $1.47, no surge, total $34.32 [F4][F5][F6]. Under RD-2's non-metered branch the only recoverable items are ERP/toll actually incurred and any unpublished add-on; the itemisation contains neither (there is no toll/ERP line and no extra charge beyond base, distance, time and platform), so the refundable amount is $0 [F6][FARE-1][RD-2].

The GPS record nevertheless establishes an unexplained deviation: the car ran 19.1 km against a 16.5 km optimal route (+2.6 km, +16%) in 29.1 min vs 21.7 min [F1][F2], and there is exactly one off-route segment, 09:07–09:14, 4.13 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.77 km, adding 2.36 km and reaching up to 1304 m from the route [F3]. No exemption applies: no traffic incident was recorded near the route in the trip window [F13], and the only congestion readings are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the AYE and CTE, which is neither an RD-4(a) incident on the replaced optimal stretch nor a band 1/2 reading, and band 4 cannot exempt on its own [F11][F12][RD-4]; weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain [F14][RD-4]. On consent, the chat is complete and fully timestamped [F9] and contains only 08:48 pickup logistics — the rider's location message and the driver's vehicle message — neither of which mentions any route or stop [F7][F8], so no rider message sent before the 09:07 segment agrees to it; the driver's post-trip claim that his GPS rerouted him is a statement, not consent [F10][RD-5]. The segment therefore counts as an unexcused deviation [F3][RD-1][RD-5], recorded on the driver's file.

No account flag follows: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, and the driver's profile shows 2 disputes with 0 upheld (route 0, no-show 0), so this case cannot make the conduct "repeated"; profile facts could not decide the main finding in any event [F16][RD-6]. The rider's near-identical profile (1 dispute, 0 upheld) is immaterial [F15][RD-6]. Because the rider was billed the fixed optimal-distance quote with no waiting fee and no unpublished add-on, the monetary outcome is nil and the ruling is no_action, with the RD-1 breach noted [F4][F6][RD-2].

Safety screen: I read every message, the driver's statement and the complaint. The chat is pickup logistics only [F7][F8][F9], the driver's statement is a fare/route denial [F10], and the complaint is a fare/route grievance; nothing reads as a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no escalation under SAFE-1/SAFE-2 arises [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the GPS deviation is measured and segmented [F1][F3], the fare is fully itemised [F6], and the chat record is complete and timestamped [F9], which is everything the ruling needs; the RD-5 scope question on F3 changes neither the amount (fixed fare, $0 recoverable) nor the flag (RD-6 predicate unmet), so it is settled here as the stipulated consent_after_or_none [F3][F7][F8][F9][RD-5].
